title: The Out-of-Towners
about: An Ohio couple's trip to New York becomes a night of non-stop disasters.
cue: Serve dessert when George finally gets to eat something.
faces: Guests take the morning air in Central Park, a short walk up Fifth.
IN YOUR ROOM, 6 A.M. TO NOON
Seared to order and rested, two eggs fried, hash browns and buttered toast.
Chilled orange juice, a warm croissant, sweet butter, preserves and a pot of coffee.
A tall stack with whipped butter, warm maple syrup and country sausage.
Poached eggs and Canadian bacon on a toasted English muffin, hollandaise.
Sliced berries, sugared lightly, with a jug of thickened cream.
Our kitchen never runs out. Taxis scarce? Ask the doorman.
Please call back in the morning.
SERVED IN YOUR ROOM UNTIL 2 A.M.
Crisp apple, celery, green grapes and toasted walnuts in a lemon mayonnaise, on butter lettuce.
Three decker, sliced turkey, bacon, lettuce and tomato on toast.
Glazed sticky with honey, mustard, brown sugar and Worcestershire, on picks with pearl onions.
Baked slowly in a water bath on a crumb crust, chilled overnight, crowned with sliced strawberries.
Butter shortbread sandwiched with raspberry jam, dusted with sugar. Boxed for the handbag.
Gin and dry vermouth stirred very cold, strained, one green olive.
Rye, sweet vermouth and bitters, stirred, with a cherry.
Fresh brewed, with cream. Serves two.
Our limousine meets every flight, fog or no fog.
George, sit down and order the steak. You have earned it.
Rooms held until 6 P.M. unless guaranteed. Please do not cross the park after dark.

Boxed for the handbag.From the pastry cart.How to make it200g soft butter120g icing sugar, plus extra to dust250g plain flour50g cornflour120g raspberry jamBeat the butter and icing sugar until pale. Mix in the flour and cornflour to a soft dough.Press into a lined 20 x 30cm tin and prick all over.Bake at 160°C until pale golden.Cut into 24 fingers while warm and cool in the tin.Sandwich pairs with jam and dust with icing sugar.Cocktail FranksGlazed sticky with honey, mustard, brown sugar and Worcestershire, on picks with pearl onions.From the kitchen, until 2 A.M.How to make it500g cocktail franks20g butter3 tbsp honey2 tbsp Dijon mustard1 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1 jar cocktail onionsSimmer the franks in water, then drain.Melt the butter with the honey, Dijon, sugar and Worcestershire in a frying pan.Add the franks and toss over medium heat until sticky and glazed.Serve on toothpicks with cocktail onions.MainsRib Eye Steak and EggsSeared to order and rested, two eggs fried, hash browns and buttered toast.Breakfast in your room, 6 A.M. to noon.How to make it600g potatoes1/2 tsp fine salt80g butter800g rib eye steak, in four pieces1 tbsp vegetable oil8 eggs4 slices of sourdoughGrate the potatoes and squeeze dry in a tea towel. Season and shape into 4 hash browns.Fry the hash browns in some of the butter over medium heat, turning once.Sear the steaks in a very hot pan with the oil to about 54°C, then rest.Fry the eggs in butter.Toast the sourdough and butter it. Serve a steak, two eggs, a hash brown and a toast each.SweetsNew York CheesecakeBaked slowly in a water bath on a crumb crust, chilled overnight, crowned with sliced strawberries.From the pastry cart.How to make it120g digestive biscuits50g butter, melted400g cream cheese100g caster sugar100g sour cream2 eggs1 tsp vanilla extract200g strawberries, slicedCrush the biscuits, mix with the butter and press into a lined 18cm springform tin.Beat the cream cheese and sugar, then mix in the sour cream, eggs and vanilla. Pour over the base.Wrap the tin in two layers of foil and stand in a roasting dish with hot water halfway up its sides.Bake at 150°C until the centre gently wobbles.Cool, then refrigerate overnight.Top with strawberries and cut into portions.DrinksDry MartiniGin and dry vermouth stirred very cold, strained, one green olive.From the bar.
